subject: Helio Diagnostics — PoC architecture, auth, embeddings & 502 repro
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@heliodx.com>, Eva Li <eva.li@heliodx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helio Diagnostics PoC — recap, architecture asks, and next steps

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap from our discovery and a set of concrete next steps so we can scope the PoC.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference for clinical note retrieval + structured extraction into Helio's triage pipeline. Embeddings for sem-search, then a light reranker to boost precision for high-priority results.
- Data: customer-hosted document store (S3 + Elasticsearch) behind a private VPC.
- Constraints: low 95th p99 latency requirement for triage UI; HIPAA + audit logging; prefer regional routing with failover.

Action items we agreed on:
1) PoC access: please confirm which env we should target (dev vs staging) and provide an API key or service account for the PoC. If you prefer mTLS, call that out and we'll switch to the private deployment guidance.
2) SDK setup & auth: we'll provide an SDK quickstart (node + python). For initial tests, API key is easiest; for final PoC we'll show how to configure KMS-backed service tokens.
3) Routing: suggest routing primary->us-west, fallback->us-east. We can show canary/fallback routing policy on the console.
4) Structured output/tool calling: you mentioned wanting to call an internal retrieval microservice for patient metadata — we'll demonstrate function/tool-calling examples and safe parsing templates.
5) Embeddings & reranker: our recommended flow is (a) precompute embeddings for docs, (b) retrieve top-K, (c) rerank with a lightweight combiner model. We'll provide a sizing estimate for embedding batch windows.

Repro note: during the brief smoke run this morning your team hit intermittent 502s when sending batches of 48 embedding requests (see attached heliodx-smoke-20270508.log and sample payload). The errors look like 5xx from our runtime rather than client validation. Please attach any server-side traces you have.

Next steps / owners:
- Helio: confirm target env + provide test credentials (Sam / Eva)
- Redwood: Priyom will own the PoC engagement and coordinate an SE deep-dive. Dev will triage the 502 repro and provide recommended config. Jordan will set up the initial billing/PO path.

I've attached the smoke log and the payload you used. Priyom / Dev — can you take the next pass on repro steps and recommend client-side tuning (timeouts, batch size) so Sam can re-run tomorrow?

Thanks,
Aisha
Sales Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- heliodx-smoke-20270508.log (log excerpt)
- heliodx-sample-payload.json (batch request sample)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Helio Diagnostics PoC — recap, architecture asks, and next steps

Looping in some quick repro steps and immediate configuration recommendations. I dug through the attached log (thanks) — the 502s are coming from the runtime when concurrent KV-cache misses coincide with large embedding batches. We should be able to avoid the symptoms with client-side tuning and a small runtime change (I'll raise an infra ticket).

Immediate repro steps (what I'll run locally):
1) curl reproducer (embedding batch):
   curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings\" \
     -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
     -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
     -d @heliodx-sample-payload.json 

   sample payload: 48 items, average length 900 chars, model=redwood-emb-v1

2) Node SDK reproducer:
   const rw = require('redwood-js');
   const client = rw({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'us-west' });
   await client.embeddings.create({model: 'redwood-emb-v1', input: batch});

Quick configuration recommendations to try before infra changes:
- Client timeout: raise from default 30s -> 60s for embedding batches (network spikes cause mid-run cancellations).
- Batch size: reduce from 48 -> 16-24 for initial runs; tune up after confirming stability.
- Concurrency: limit parallel embedding requests to 3 per connection.
- Use sticky routing to a single instance (region: us-west) for the run to reduce cross-instance KV misses (set routing.prefer_local_cache = true).
- If you need lower p99, use our dedicated pooling recommendation (Reserved capacity).

Runtime suggestion (short term): I'll file JIRA SUP-2984 for the KV cold-start path that surfaced here; infra may land a hotfix to soften the failure mode.

If the 502 reproduces with the small batch + 60s timeout, send me the X-Request-ID header values from the failed responses (e.g., X-Request-ID: 0xabc123). That will let me correlate to logs.

Attachment: none (used aisha's attachments).

-Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
